title: Leaf: readReviewLedgers collects journaled landing-intent keys in its existing decision walk, fail-closed on a malformed intent
description:
SPIDR LEAF spun out of task-f7d38f752b074dc89da30631783aae04 ("a node that legitimately lands nothing never counts toward its goal") by architect-ed42e60a, 2026-09-10, on governor-608c8a78's correction (msg-3623a98c): the parent's amendment had grown to 12 effective paths and documented a fail-OPEN edge. This leaf carries the three paths the parent could not, and the fail-CLOSED rule. The parent declares this row in dependsOn and consumes what it lands.

WHY IT EXISTS. The parent's landed predicate `landedWithNoEffect(receipt)` (landing-receipt-contracts.ts:38-39) credits a NOTHING_TO_COMMIT landing by CODE ALONE. architect-978f68c6 reproduced through the real runtime (parent comment-573c4f2c, reproducer comment-d5730986) that a retry after a journaled intent, with the node's file reverted, yields the same code: `{"outcome":"REFUSED","code":"NOTHING_TO_COMMIT","deliveryFacts":"REFUSED","credited":true}` — lost work credited as landed. The corrected rule is the code AND no journaled landing intent for that acceptance. The intent is durable and handle-free: every intent is a committed decision of commandKind `internal.repository.landing_intent` (repository-landing-intent.ts:12, module-private literal; written by writeRecoveryFact) whose decoded body carries `nodeRef` and `verifierReceiptId` (decodeRepositoryLandingIntent is already exported, :24-35). All three of the parent's seams already call `readReviewLedgers` (review-read-model.ts:288-322), which walks every decision once via `decisionsOf(store, LEDGER_PAGE_SIZE)` at :303 — collecting intent keys in that walk is one pass, zero extra cost, and avoids a second full-ledger scan on the affordance hot path (the daemon loop was measured pegged by full scans before, fixed at ec604baa).

WHAT THIS LEAF LANDS, three files:
1. repository-landing-intent.ts: EXPORT the intent kind literal (today `const INTENT_KIND = "internal.repository.landing_intent"` at :12) and a `landingIntentKey(nodeRef, verifierReceiptId)` helper so the key is spelled once.
2. review-read-model.ts (332 lines): in the :303 walk, for EFFECTS_COMMITTED decisions of that kind, decode `resultBytes` with `decodeRepositoryLandingIntent`; collect the keys into a new frozen `landingIntents` on `ReviewLedgers`. FAIL CLOSED: if ANY such decision fails to decode, `landingIntents` is `null` — "unverifiable evidence gains no authority". The parent's predicate treats null as "credit nothing". Do not narrow this by "the writer round-trip-validates so it cannot happen" — that is reachability prose, not a boundary.
3. review-read-model.test.ts: (a) a real intent written through the PRODUCTION writer (recordRepositoryLandingIntent with a reservation handle from createRepositoryExecutionPort, the way repository-delivery-runtime.test.ts:23-66 builds one) appears in `landingIntents` under the exact key; (b) a decision of the intent kind whose bytes do NOT decode (seed via store.commitExpectedVersionDecision with the kind literal and junk resultBytes) makes `landingIntents` null; (c) an intent for a different verifierReceiptId does not match a receipt's key (the parent's positive control depends on this); (d) `landings` and `ledgers` are byte-identical to before for a store with no intents — the existing arms stay green.

NOT IN THIS LEAF: the predicate change, the three seams, the runtime proof arm — those are the parent's, against its nine checkpointed paths plus repository-delivery-runtime.test.ts.
definitionOfDone: review-read-model.ts returns `landingIntents: ReadonlySet<string> | null` collected in the SAME decisionsOf walk as `landings` — an arm counts decision pages read and proves no second walk was added.

A landing intent written through the production writer appears in landingIntents under `landingIntentKey(nodeRef, verifierReceiptId)`; an intent for a different verifierReceiptId does not match — both asserted by key content.

A committed decision of the intent kind whose resultBytes do not decode makes landingIntents `null` (fail closed), asserted as null and not as an empty set; deleting the null branch in production makes this arm RED (drill recorded with SHA256 restore proof, task id in the backup path).

The intent kind literal is exported from repository-landing-intent.ts and spelled in exactly one place: `git grep -n 'internal.repository.landing_intent' -- apps/daemon/src` returns only that definition plus imports.
Existing review-read-model arms pass unedited; pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test EXIT 0 with its Test Files count line quoted.

implementationPlan.description:
EXPORT THE KIND AND THE KEY (repository-landing-intent.ts) (DoD 4).

Export the existing module-private `INTENT_KIND` at :12 so the review model imports it instead of retyping it, and add `landingIntentKey(nodeRef, verifierReceiptId)` so the key is spelled ONCE and both producer and consumer cannot disagree about its shape.

CHOOSE A KEY THAT CANNOT COLLIDE. `nodeRef` is free-form text bounded only by `ref()` at :16 (non-empty, <= 4096, no control characters), so a naive `${nodeRef}:${verifierReceiptId}` is ambiguous if a nodeRef contains the separator. `verifierReceiptId` is `hex()` — exactly 64 lowercase hex — so putting the FIXED-WIDTH field first, or using a separator that `ref()` forbids, makes the encoding unambiguous. Say in a comment which property makes it safe; a key helper whose safety is accidental is one refactor from a silent collision.

DO NOT change `decodeRepositoryLandingIntent`, the intent id derivation, or anything the writer uses. This step widens the module's exports and adds one pure helper; it changes no behaviour.

DoD 4's GATE: after this, `git grep -n "internal.repository.landing_intent" -- apps/daemon/src` returns the definition plus imports and nothing else. A second spelling anywhere passes every behavioural arm and fails this gate.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 2 DONE — repository-landing-intent.ts, 102 -> 121 lines (cap-safe).

KIND EXPORTED, NOT ALIASED. The module-private `const INTENT_KIND` is GONE, replaced by `export const REPOSITORY_LANDING_INTENT_KIND = "internal.repository.landing_intent";` (:17), and the three internal uses (writeRecoveryFact at :83, readRecoveryFact at :90 and :107) now name the exported constant directly. I deliberately did NOT keep a private alias pointing at the export: one kind with two names is exactly the drift the DoD-4 gate is written against, and the file's existing lines already run to ~180 chars so the longer names cost nothing.

KEY HELPER, AND WHY IT CANNOT COLLIDE. `landingIntentKey(nodeRef, verifierReceiptId) => `${verifierReceiptId}:${nodeRef}`` — RECEIPT ID FIRST. That ordering is the safety property, stated in the comment rather than left to convention: `verifierReceiptId` is validated by `hex()` (exactly 64 lowercase hex characters, so it can hold neither the separator nor anything else), while `nodeRef` is bounded only by `ref()` (non-empty, <= 4096 chars, no control characters) and MAY contain a colon. With the free-form field first, `("a:b","c")` and `("a","b:c")` collapse to one string; with the fixed-width field first the key always splits at index 64 and the pair round-trips for ANY nodeRef. Placed below the `intentId`/`aggregate`/`completionId` derivation cluster so the constants stay together.

NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGED: `decodeRepositoryLandingIntent`, `intentId`, `aggregate`, `completionId` and every writer path are byte-identical apart from the constant's name.

The package's own `test` script is the only correct invocation.)

implementationPlan.description:
COLLECT THE KEYS IN THE EXISTING WALK, FAIL CLOSED (review-read-model.ts) (DoD 1, DoD 3).

Add `landingIntents: ReadonlySet<string> | null` to `ReviewLedgers` at :275-281 and to the frozen return at :321. Populate it inside the loop at :303, after the `EFFECTS_COMMITTED` guard: for a decision whose `commandKind` is the imported intent kind, decode `resultBytes` with `decodeRepositoryLandingIntent` and add `landingIntentKey(intent.nodeRef, intent.verifierReceiptId)`.

COLLECT EVERY PROJECT INTENT — do NOT narrow by `landingSubjects` the way the landing-receipt branch does. The key is the exact pair, lookups are exact, and the nodeRef is only known AFTER decoding, so a subject filter would decode and then discard: all cost, no saving, plus a subtle failure where an intent for a subject this caller did not name is dropped and the parent later asks about it.

FAIL CLOSED, AND THIS IS THE CLAUSE THE ROW EXISTS FOR. If ANY decision of that kind fails to decode, `landingIntents` is `null` — not an empty set. Empty means "walked, found none"; null means "unverifiable, credit nothing", and the parent's predicate treats null as crediting nothing. Do NOT narrow this to "the writer round-trip-validates so it cannot happen": that is reachability prose, not a boundary, and the leaf forbids it in writing.

SET A FLAG, NEVER RETURN EARLY. The walk must complete: `landings`, `ledgers`, `receipts` and `decisionCount` (which `ledgerOf` consumes at :318) all depend on it. Null the set after the loop.

ONE PASS, AND IT MUST BE PROVABLE. DoD 1 wants an arm that counts decision pages read and would FAIL if someone later adds a convenience scan — so leave the counting seam in a shape a test can observe rather than an argument in a comment.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 3 DONE — review-read-model.ts, 332 -> 362 lines (+31/-1). Under the 400 split bar; the file was already past the 250 target before this row, and the addition is 31 lines of which 17 are comment.

SHAPE: `ReviewLedgers` gains `readonly landingIntents: ReadonlySet<string> | null` as its FIRST member, with the null-vs-empty distinction written into the doc comment rather than left for a reader to infer — empty means "walked the ledger, found no intent, crediting on the receipt code alone is safe"; null means "an intent was journaled and its bytes are unreadable, credit nothing".

COLLECTION SITE: inside the SAME `for (const decision of decisionsOf(store, LEDGER_PAGE_SIZE))` loop, after the `EFFECTS_COMMITTED` guard, beside the landing-receipt branch. No second walk, no second `decisionsOf` call. NOT narrowed by `landingSubjects` — comment on the branch says why: the key is the exact pair and the nodeRef is known only AFTER decoding, so a subject filter would decode and then discard, and would silently drop an intent a later caller asks about.

FAIL CLOSED: `intentUnreadable` flag set inside the loop, never a `return`. The comment at the branch names what an early return would break: `landings`, `receipts`, and the `decisionCount` that `ledgerOf` stamps onto EVERY subject's ledger in the batch. The set is nulled after the loop, in the frozen return: `landingIntents: intentUnreadable ? null : landingIntents`.

DECODE CHAIN, which the plan did not spell out: `decodeRepositoryLandingIntent` takes a decoded value, not bytes, so the call is `decodeRepositoryLandingIntent(decodeResult(decision.resultBytes))` using the module's existing `decodeResult` (:75-78). It fails closed on BOTH legs — unparseable bytes give `null`, and `decodeRepositoryLandingIntent(null)` is `null` because its `record()` guard rejects null. No "the writer round-trip-validates so this cannot happen" narrowing anywhere.

THE ONE-PASS SEAM (DoD 1) NEEDED NO PRODUCTION CHANGE and I checked rather than assumed: `decisionsOf` reads pages exclusively through `store.readCommandDecisionsAfter`, so a proxy store counting that call observes pages read — the `countingStore` pattern already in goal-landing-facts.test.ts:249-290. implementationPlan.description:
THE ARMS, THE DRILL, AND THE GATE (DoD 1, 2, 3, 5).

(a) REAL INTENT, PRODUCTION WRITER (DoD 2): write an intent through `recordRepositoryLandingIntent` with a reservation handle from `createRepositoryExecutionPort`, built the way repository-delivery-runtime.test.ts:23-66 builds one, and assert it appears in `landingIntents` under `landingIntentKey(nodeRef, verifierReceiptId)`. Assert the KEY CONTENT, not set size — a size assertion passes for the wrong key.

(b) WRONG RECEIPT DOES NOT MATCH (DoD 2): an intent for a DIFFERENT verifierReceiptId is absent from the lookup for this receipt's key. The parent's positive control depends on this, so it is not optional colour.

(c) FAIL CLOSED (DoD 3): seed a committed decision of the intent kind with junk `resultBytes` via `store.commitExpectedVersionDecision`, and assert `landingIntents` is `null` — asserted AS NULL, explicitly, not as an empty set. Those two are different claims and only one is the safe one.

(d) ONE PASS (DoD 1): count decision pages read and prove no second walk was added. This arm must be able to FAIL — if you cannot make it fail by adding a scan, it is an argument rather than a test.

(e) NO REGRESSION (DoD 5): `landings` and `ledgers` are byte-identical for a store with no intents, and the existing arms in review-read-model.test.ts pass UNEDITED. That is the cheapest proof the widening changed nothing.

THE DRILL (DoD 3): delete the null branch in production and confirm arm (c) goes RED. Before mutating, `git status --porcelain` the path, copy it out of tree to `%TEMP%` under a name carrying BOTH this task id and your worker id, and record the SHA256 taken FROM THE LIVE FILE. Restore by copying the backup back and prove it by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore. A backup keyed only on a seat id can hold a stale vintage from an earlier session.

GATE: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, FOREGROUND and STANDALONE, exit code AND the `Test Files N passed` count line quoted verbatim and nonzero. Read the OUTPUT, not the exit code. Run `pnpm typecheck` too — this widens an exported interface that eight call sites consume.

COMPLETION RECORD: state that the parent's predicate, the three seams and the runtime proof arm are deliberately NOT here, so a grader does not read a `landingIntents` nobody consumes yet as incomplete work. The parent declares this row in dependsOn and consumes it.

full-suite-gate is held by worker-b42eccd4 / task-9255156954724b7dbbcbf03ae2aaa11c (acquired 10:02:39Z, live, docker-compose port-exclusive work). (a) ONE undecodable intent nulls the set for the WHOLE PROJECT, not just its node — so a single corrupt intent stops the parent crediting EVERY landing in that project. That is what the row's "if ANY such decision fails to decode" mandates and it is the safe direction, but the blast radius is felt in the parent's predicate, not here.
(b) `landingIntents` is not bounded by `subjectRefs` the way `landings` is, so it grows with the project's whole intent history. Bounded in practice by the fact that `decisionsOf` already materialises every CommandDecisionRecord (resultBytes included) for the same walk — the key set is a rounding error against the memo it rides on.
Also noted: `Object.freeze` on the returned object does NOT make the Set immutable (freeze has no effect on Set internals). The member is typed `ReadonlySet<string>` and the container is frozen, which is exactly how `landings`/`ledgers`/`receipts` already behave; freezing the Set itself would be theatre.

THE LEAF'S OWN DESIGN IS ADOPTED — collect intent keys inside the EXISTING `decisionsOf` walk, fail closed on a malformed intent. It is right and the reasoning holds: all three of the parent's seams already call `readReviewLedgers`, so one pass costs nothing and a second full-ledger scan on the affordance hot path is exactly what was measured pegging the daemon loop before (fixed at ec604baa).

REJECTED — exposing a count or a boolean instead of the key set. The parent needs to answer "was there an intent for THIS acceptance", which is a membership question. A count cannot answer it and a boolean answers a different one.

2. `null` IS NOT AN EMPTY SET, and DoD 3 says so explicitly. An empty set means "walked, found none, credit by code alone is safe"; null means "unverifiable, credit nothing". Returning an empty set on a decode failure is the fail-OPEN edge this leaf exists to close, and it would pass a careless arm.

3. THE DRILL IS THE PROOF THE BRANCH IS LOAD-BEARING (DoD 3). Deleting the null branch must make the arm RED. Back the file up out of tree under a name carrying BOTH this task id and your worker id, take the SHA256 from the LIVE file before mutating, restore by copying back, and prove it by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore.

4. DO NOT RETYPE THE KIND LITERAL. DoD 4 gates on the grep returning only the definition plus imports. A second spelling in the review model passes every behavioural arm and fails that gate.

5. THE "NO SECOND WALK" ARM (DoD 1) NEEDS A REAL COUNTER, not an argument. Count decision pages read, or instrument `decisionsOf`, so the arm would FAIL if someone later adds a convenience scan. An arm that merely asserts the result is correct cannot see a second pass.

7. THE PARENT IS A SEPARATE ROW. The predicate change, the three seams and the runtime proof arm are NOT in this leaf. Landing a `landingIntents` nobody reads yet is correct here — the parent declares this row in dependsOn and consumes it.
